subject: Growth Model with Dichotomous Outcome Using Theta Parameterization

messages.author: 7fea0091ab5e68ab
messages.subject: Growth Model with Dichotomous Outcome Using Theta Parameterization
parts:
I'm getting an error message when specifying a linear growth model for a dichotomous outcome using the theta parameterization. Here's my code and the error message:

> cat = c('write1','write2','write3','write4')

> theta_constrain<-'

eta_0 =~ 1*write1+1*write2+1*write3+1*write4
eta_1 =~ 0*write1+1*write2+3*write3+5*write4
eta_0 ~ 0*1
eta_1 ~ 1
eta_0 ~~ eta_0
eta_1 ~~ eta_1
eta_0 ~~ eta_1

#Thresholds
write1|tau*t1
write2|tau*t1
write3|tau*t1
write4|tau*t1

write1 ~~ 1*write1
write2 ~~ 1*write2
write3 ~~ 1*write3
write4 ~~ 1*write4
'

> theta_constrain_fit<-lavaan(theta_constrain,data=faces,ordered=cat,parameterization='theta',estimator='wlsmv')

Error in MLIST$delta[, 1L] <- sqrt(1/tmp) : 
  incorrect number of subscripts on matrix

Any ideas?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Growth Model with Dichotomous Outcome Using Theta Parameterization
parts:
On 06/20/2015 06:32 AM, Kevin J Grimm wrote:
> theta_constrain_fit<-lavaan(theta_constrain,data=faces,ordered=cat,parameterization='theta',estimator='wlsmv')
>
> Error in MLIST$delta[, 1L] <- sqrt(1/tmp) :
> incorrect number of subscripts on matrix

Yes. If parameterization = "theta", lavaan() also needs the 'delta'
parameters (although they are fixed to one), and they are not added by
default (something I will change in a future update).

So, in your syntax, add the following 4 lines:

write1 ~*~ 1*write1
write2 ~*~ 1*write2
write3 ~*~ 1*write3
write4 ~*~ 1*write4

(or use the sem() function).

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Growth Model with Dichotomous Outcome Using Theta Parameterization

> Error in MLIST$delta[, 1L] <- sqrt(1/tmp) :
> incorrect number of subscripts on matrix

I changed this in dev 0.5-19.863. The 'delta' parameters are now always
added by default, even if you use the lavaan() function.

Yves.
